clue.text: Inferred what Tom Daley did, perhaps, captivates the Queen

indicators.note: to captivate is pictured as holding something captive inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Tom Daley is a British Olympic diver, so what he did was dive into the pool
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A sports fan concludes something about the Olympic diver and his royal admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Daley is a British Olympic diving champion; 'perhaps' warns that this is one example of the past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a conclusion drawn from evidence is one that has been deduced or obtained from it.

clue.text: Churchman of French origin in Alcatraz with prisoner

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: origin in says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A French-born chaplain ministers in Alcatraz alongside a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchman in holy orders ranking below a priest, or a lay church officer.

clue.text: Match official bungle oddly ignored safety

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is a match official

indicators.note: oddly ignored says the first, third and fifth letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A referee's blunder ignored player safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter or haven is a place of safety, protection from danger.

clue.text: Offers kinky nurse love? About time!

indicators.note: About says the rearranged letters go round the letter for time
kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky patient asks a nurse for affection and is told it is about time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps VOLUNEERS (the anagram of NURSE LOVE, from 'kinky') around T.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to step forward and put oneself forward freely is to offer.

clue.text: Kent town's bargains

definitions.meaning: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, England; with the apostrophe it reads as its name plus 's
agreements or transactions, as in business

explanation.definitionFit: A Kentish coastal town's name plus 's, and business agreements struck between parties.

clue.text: Page to be first, editor begged

parts.note: to lead is to be in first place in a race

explanation.surface: A newspaper page wants to be up front, and its editor pleads for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to beg and to plead both mean to ask earnestly for something.

clue.text: Plant I vote to be uprooted? Not very likely

indicators.note: a plant uprooted is torn up and disturbed, so these letters are rearranged
Not says the letter for very is not part of the rearranged result

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether voting to dig up a plant will pass: not very likely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be uprooted' rearranges PLANT I VOTE, and 'Not very' takes the V out of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means possible or likely to develop in future, latent.

clue.text: Rake in bottom of garden under part of cereal plant

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the second piece below the first

parts.note: the ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant

indicators.note: bottom of picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A gardener rakes at the bottom of the garden under some cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to rake in money is to make a lot of it, to gain it as income.

clue.text: Small drink of alcohol and a jerk gets theatrical

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A tipsy person jerks about and becomes rather theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: overdone, showy behaviour suited to the stage is theatrical.

clue.text: Maybe relish putting on clothes

definitions.meaning: a sauce or condiment such as a salad topping; relish is one example, hence maybe

explanation.definitionFit: A sauce poured over food, and the act of clothing oneself.

clue.text: A wife almost generous? Rubbish!

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a generous helping is a full one

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a wife could be nearly generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive verdicts: calling something dreadful is to say it is no good, like crying rubbish.

clue.text: Every second a flyer goes in behind schedule

indicators.note: goes in says the bird is placed inside the word for late

parts.note: behind schedule means late
a tern is a seabird, a flyer

explanation.surface: An airline passenger, or a bird, arrives late every second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens on alternate days happens every other one, every second occasion.

clue.text: Arranging musical instrument, one with whistle

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument
I is the Roman numeral one
a kettle that whistles is said to sing

explanation.surface: A musician arranges a piece for organ and one whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: setting things in order or planning an event is arranging it.

clue.text: Friends hit back

indicators.note: back says the word for hit is read in the other direction

parts.note: to slap is to hit

explanation.surface: Friends retaliate when one of them is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: mates and chums are close companions.

clue.text: Goes around North with German travellers

indicators.note: around says the word for goes wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: goes by is passes

explanation.surface: Someone travels round the north of the country with a German companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Those riding in a vehicle, not driving it, are its travellers.

clue.text: Exotic Persia trip? No sweat

indicators.note: exotic suggests something foreign and strange, so these letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A traveller to Persia insists the trip was easy: no sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No sweat' reads as a phrase meaning 'no trouble', but 'No' joins the anagram and 'sweat' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the moisture the skin gives off in heat is sweat.

clue.text: Rugby perhaps popular with good training

parts.note: Rugby is a famous English public school, where the sport was born
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Rugby is thought popular as good physical training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby' suggests the sport; it is Rugby School, the English private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: education or instruction received is training.

clue.text: Attack that crosses a line?

parts.note: an assault that goes over a border, read also as overstepping the mark

explanation.definitionFit: A military incursion into another country's territory means crossing its frontier.

clue.text: All evening Ray loses heart with me

parts.note: eve is a poetic word for evening

indicators.note: loses heart says the middle letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, a name or a beam
one can stand for oneself, i.e. me

explanation.surface: Ray spends a whole evening downhearted with the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: every single person is all of them.

clue.text: Despite everything, even shelter's damaged

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of these words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: People carry on even though their shelter has been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: all the same, regardless of everything, is what the adverb means.

clue.text: 'Poking it out' could be considered rude language

definitions.text: 'Poking it out' could be considered rude
definitions.meaning: sticking out the organ of the mouth is a rude gesture
a ... is a language, as in mother ...

explanation.definitionFit: The mouth organ one sticks out cheekily, and a spoken language.

clue.text: Snake starts to emerge, checking the air

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A snake comes out and tests the air with its tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a look or appearance, as in an air of mystery, is an aspect.

clue.text: Couples softly dropped voices

indicators.note: dropped says the letter for softly is taken out of the word for couples

parts.note: couples are pairs
P, piano, is the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Duet partners lower their voices to a hush.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to give an opinion an airing is to voice it, express it publicly.

clue.text: I count on us working uninterrupted

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A manager tells the team they are relied on to keep working without breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something unbroken and ceaseless goes on without interruption.

clue.text: Rendered notes?

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters are reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: A query about notes that have been performed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: notes when sung or played become sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical sounds of definite pitch are what notes become when performed.

clue.text: Extract from Rimbaud a little surrealist

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reader quotes a short passage of Rimbaud's poetry, much admired by surrealists.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador, the Spanish painter of melting clocks, was the best-known surrealist.

clue.text: I note a duck is in container for quarantine

parts.note: sol (or so) is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: is in says the duck sits inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a container
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a duck is being kept in a box to stop disease spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is a period of enforced separation, keeping the possibly infected apart from others.

clue.text: Keen to ignore tail, holding large bird

indicators.note: holding says the shortened word wraps round the letter for large
to ignore tail says the last letter of the word for keen is left off

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: A keen birdwatcher grips a large bird while ignoring its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore tail' removes R from EAGER, leaving EAGE, which then holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the golden one is a large bird of prey, a raptor.

clue.text: Requiring massaging, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for massaging is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: massaging dough or muscles is kneading them

explanation.surface: Someone's sore back seems to call for a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: wanting or lacking something essential is requiring it.

clue.text: Questionable American power in religious community

indicators.note: in says those letters go inside the religious community

parts.note: a sect is a religious community
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An American gaining power in a religious group seems dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something dubious or open to doubt is questionable.
